routes.label: Bound the 14-step difference, then use endpoint inequalities to determine the sequence

question:
Fifteen integers \(a_1,\) \(a_2,\) \(a_3,\) \(\cdots,\) \(a_{15}\) are arranged in order on a number line. The integers are equally spaced and have the property that

\[ 1 \leq a_1 \leq 10, \]

\[ 13 \leq a_2 \leq 20, \]

and

\[ 241 \leq a_{15} \leq 250. \]

What is the sum of the digits of \(a_{14}?\)
solution:
Fifteen equally spaced numbers create \(14\) equal gaps. Comparing the first and last numbers combines all those gaps, which will help us find the size of one step. Let \(d\) be the size of one step. Since the numbers are integers, \(d\) is an integer, and

\[
a_{15}-a_1=14d.
\]

To bound the total distance, use the endpoint ranges. The last number is at least \(241\) and the first is at most \(10\), so their difference is at least \(241-10=231\). It is at most \(250-1=249\). Therefore

\[
231\leq 14d\leq 249.
\]

The neighboring multiples of \(14\) are \(224\), \(238\), and \(252\). Only \(238\) lies in this interval, so \(14d=238\) and \(d=17\).

Now use the other bounds to find the starting number. Since

\[
a_2=a_1+17\leq 20,
\]

we get \(a_1\leq 3\). Also,

\[
a_{15}=a_1+238\geq 241,
\]

so \(a_1\geq 3\). Together these force \(a_1=3\), giving \(a_2=20\) and \(a_{15}=241\). These values satisfy all three given ranges.

Move back one step from \(a_{15}\) to find

\[
a_{14}=241-17=224.
\]

Its digit sum is \(2+2+4=\boxed{8}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).

For equally spaced integers, count the gaps first. Bounds on distant terms can pin down the common step, and the remaining bounds can then locate the whole sequence.
